newsitem.title: UK: Britain criticises Burma jail sentences.
newsitem.headline: Britain criticises Burma jail sentences.

text.p: Britain accused Burma's military government on Wednesday of imposing harsh jail sentences on 14 people for involvement in student unrest and urged it to respect human rights.
The 14, including five members of opposition leader Aung San Suu Kyi's National League for Democracy (NLD), were each jailed for seven years for involvement in last month's student unrest.
The military government said on Tuesday they were found guilty of agitation and throwing rocks at security personnel.
A British Foreign Office spokesman said: "We deplore the harsh sentences imposed by the State Law and Order Restoration Council (SLORC) on 14 people arrested last month during student protests.
"We are particularly concerned that these trials were not free and fair and call on SLORC to ensure full respect for human rights in Burma."

Thousands of Rangoon university students launched anti-government street protests in the capital in December to seek greater freedoms. More than 800 students were briefly detained for taking part in the protests.
The protests were the biggest in the capital since the pro-democracy uprising of 1988, which was crushed by the military and left thousands dead or in jail.
